thread.title: Boston Properties: Double Your Yield And Add A Layer Of Protection With This Class A REIT - Boston Properties, Inc. (NYSE:BXP)

author: Income Machine
title: Boston Properties: Double Your Yield And Add A Layer Of Protection With This Class A REIT - Boston Properties, Inc. (NYSE:BXP)
text:
As a conservative income investor, I seek securities that offer a compelling mix of high yield and low risk. Unfortunately, the market rarely serves an appetizing platter offering them both up at once. You don’t get to devour cheesecake and have it digest like a salad. You pick your poison.
You either accept greater risk for a juicier yield, or you sacrifice yield for a safer play. The stock market is efficient enough to price securities accordingly. When mispriced opportunities materialize, they rarely last long.
Fortunately for you and I, "last long" can entail just enough time to swing by and scoop up shares before the weighing machine of the market corrects the discrepancy. Let me highlight one such opportunity hiding in plain sight.
Boston Properties ( BXP ) is one of the largest owners of Class A office properties in the country. You may have read about it recently when it unveiled the new Salesforce Tower in San Francisco. The building is remarkable, as it’s the tallest rooftop west of Chicago. Salesforce (NYSE: CRM ) signed a 15.-year lease back in 2014 which granted it naming rights over the building during that period. Quotes from both Salesforce and Boston Properties indicate that the relationship between landlord and tenant has been very collaborative and cooperative.
Boston Properties also has significant exposure in other marquee markets like Los Angeles, New York, Washington, D.C., and of course, Boston. This is not a secondary market REIT. In total, the company owns 186 properties with over 45 million square feet of office space. Occupancy currently stands at 91.1%. The company has a market cap of $21 billion, with an average lease term of 7.3 years based on the latest 3Q investor presentation.
Why Do I Like Boston Properties? The more research I do on Boston Properties, the more I like it. To draw out a few of those reasons, the company has great credit ratings:
( Source )
Having a high credit rating keeps the cost of capital in check, which is an integral component to running a successful REIT. Part of the reason for that stellar credit rating is due to a dividend payout ratio that sits at 78%. While net debt/EBITDA sits at about 6.7x (on the high side), the fixed charge coverage ratio is approximately 3x. Management is focused on improving the leverage ratios in order to maintain the strong credit. Recently, the company issued $1 billion in green bonds . Sustainability is important to the company (and its tenants), and the cost of debt at 4.5% was relatively inexpensive.
Another reason I like Boston Properties is due to its focus on booming urban markets and the diversity and quality of its tenant pool. Tenants include Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), the United States Government, Biogen (NASDAQ: BIIB ), Bank of America (NYSE: BAC ), Smithsonian, WeWork ( VWORK ), and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), to name a few. No individual tenant comprises more than 3.2% of total revenue.
The third reason I like the company is due to its performance and alignment with shareholders. In September, Boston Properties announced a 19% increase to its dividend. Revenue growth was up 4.3% for the quarter, and that trend was intact for the previous quarters as well. Morningstar assigns a stewardship rating of "exemplary" on the company. And finally the market is taking note, sending the common share price soaring from $115 in October to $131 today.
And that is where the divergence comes into play.
The Divergence As shares of the common stock catapult up the skyline like the Salesforce Tower, the lone preferred issuance, BXP.PB has drifted down day after day. Take a peek below, with the preferred shares contrasted in orange:
I found this peculiar for a couple of reasons. First, the Federal Reserve (perhaps succumbing to political pressure) has been increasingly dovish in its remarks. While the market is pricing in another 25 basis point hike in December, the 2019 forecast is decidedly less hawkish than it was just a few months ago. This sent the 10-year Treasury south toward 3% over the past month:
(Source: CNBC )
Preferred issuances, like debt instruments, often inversely follow the 10-year note higher or lower. However, instead of the share price of the preferred moving up toward its call price of $25 over the past month, it has fallen all the way to about $22. The share price settled Friday afternoon at $22.10, representing a 13% discount to its call price.
Below are some specifics on the issuance:
(Source: Quantom Online )
Another thing that struck me about this divergence was that the company reported strong earnings and increased the common dividend. That typically signals that the preferred share is quite safe, and as you can see above, the issuance itself is investment grade with a BBB rating. Nevertheless, the share price started to fall fairly quickly after the common dividend was raised.
The stripped yield for preferred shares is currently 5.94%, or practically 6%, which is over double that of the common dividend (2.9%) even after the raise. In addition, investors are protected with a layer of safety, as preferred holders must be paid before common shareholders.
The dividend is cumulative and is trading past its call date of March, 2018. It is possible this dividend will remain outstanding for many years if interest rates continue to rise. Since the coupon rate is so low at 5.25%, I anticipate this as a distinct possibility, so potential shareholders should beware that this issuance could become a perpetuity. If the company does decide to call it, shareholders will receive a 13% premium for any shares purchased at today’s price.
I prefer to invest in preferred shares where I wouldn’t mind owning shares of the common stock, and that rings true for Boston Properties. The recent divergence highlighted above allowed me to juice the yield while adding a layer of protection, and that was an opportunity worth pursuing, in my estimation. In today’s elevated market, I am content receiving 6% with a level of safety, which is why I purchased shares of the preferred stock, BXP.PB, this week.
Disclosure: I am/we are long BXP.PB.
